fields.title: Unicorn membership contract
fields.body_md:
## 1. Statute of the association (the post box)

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

Unicorn e.V. is a registered association that acts only as a post box. It holds no money and no assets, has no bank account and sells nothing. It acts only when the members have voted for it in the app, and it signs only what a vote has approved. Every person with a Unicorn account is a member, and nobody else. A small board of unpaid signers, elected and replaceable by vote, signs where the law needs a name. You must be at least 18 years old.

## 2. Trust agreement for the trade fund

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

The trade fund is the euros that members hold for the group in their own bank accounts. Held euros belong to the group, not to the holder, and are passed on when the members' decision asks for it. Holders may hold only up to their cap. Unicorn never moves money and never reads bank accounts: it shows payment requests, and the payer and the receiver confirm them. A holder who leaves first passes their part to other holders. Donations never earn UNIQ.

## 3. Consent to the tax paperwork

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

Unicorn pays taxes as the law requires. By signing, you agree that the group may prepare the tax statements that your sales to outside customers and your held euros make necessary, and that the data needed for them is used for that purpose only.

## 4. Privacy notice

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

Unicorn keeps only the personal data it needs. Your legal name, address, phone, date of birth and bank details are stored encrypted with a key of your own, apart from your hour account, which uses only your member number. You can see and download all your data, correct it, and delete your account. Deleting destroys your key. Your member number and its history stay in the open books, because the law requires the books to be kept. There is no tracking and no advertising.

## 5. Rules of the trust rating

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

The trust rating only limits how many euros you may hold for the trade fund. It never touches your work, your pay, your votes or any price. It is computed from the fund's records only. Members cannot rate each other. You can see your rating, contest it, and get a human review.

fields.title: Holder agreement
fields.body_md:
## 1. What a holder is

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

A holder is a verified member who keeps part of the trade fund in their own bank account. The euros you hold belong to the group, not to you. They are not your income and not your savings.

## 2. Passing the euros on

You send the held euros on when a decision of the members asks for it: a payment request tells you the amount, the receiver, the reference and the date. You pay it, and you and the receiver both confirm it in the app. Unicorn never moves money and never reads your bank account.

## 3. A separate account

You keep the held euros in a separate account where possible, so that the group's euros are never mixed with your own. You give the app the account number so that it can be shown to the people who pay you, and it is stored encrypted.

## 4. Caps and trust

You may hold only up to your cap. Your cap starts small and grows slowly when you pay on time. It falls fast when a payment is late or missed. The trust rating behind it only limits how many euros you may hold; it never touches your work, pay, votes or prices. You can see it, contest it and get a human review.

## 5. The loss reserve

A small share of every amount that comes in is marked as a loss reserve, kept by the holders with the highest trust. It covers thefts and missed payments, so that members' bills and materials are not hit.

## 6. Leaving

If you want to stop being a holder, or leave Unicorn, you first pass your part on to other holders, and the receivers confirm it.

fields.title: Outside seller terms
fields.body_md:
## 1. You sell in your own name

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

When you switch on outside sales, the sale, the invoice and the VAT are yours, not the group's and not the association's. Unicorn only helps you to keep the records.

## 2. Your name and address appear on invoices

The name and address you give are shown to your customers on invoices and in the imprint of your offers. They are stored encrypted.

## 3. Your own taxes

You pay your own taxes from the tax reserve: the share of every sale that you keep back for them. You may change the share with a written reason. Most members fall under the small-business rule (§ 19 UStG); Unicorn warns you when you come near its limits.

## 4. The set-aside belongs to the group

After the tax reserve, the rest of each sale is set aside. It is part of the trade fund: it is held in your holding for the group and passed on by decisions of the members. A small share is marked as loss reserve.

fields.title: Consent to be helped
fields.body_md:
## Consent to be helped

**DRAFT — to be written with lawyers (docs/12, section 2)**

I ask the helper named in this consent to act for me in Unicorn, because I cannot or do not want to use a device myself. The helper may do only what is ticked in this consent, and only until the date written in it.

Everything the helper does for me is marked "on behalf of" and I can read it under "My account, Done for me". Every month I get a summary of it.

The helper can never vote for me, sit as one of the random confirmers for me, approve hours, hold or move euros for the trade fund, sign a contract for me, change my bank details or delete my account. These I do myself.

I can end this consent at any time, and so can the helper. It ends by itself on the date written in it. A helper may help only a few members at the same time.
